explicit_propositions.text: God sacrificed His only begotten, sinless Son to atone for human sins.
The Word of God provides everything necessary for human life on Earth.
God created humans in His own image.
Every event in human life—past, present, or future—is covered by the blood of Jesus.
Those who surrender to God receive eternal life.
Surrendering oneself completely to God leads to experiencing the greatest love.
The speaker expects listeners to have a Bible, pen, and paper ready during the sermon.

assumptions.text: Human beings are inherently sinful and require redemption.
The Bible is the authoritative source of divine truth and guidance.
Salvation through Christ’s sacrifice is universally applicable and effective.
Spiritual transformation requires personal surrender and submission to God.
Pastoral preaching is a divinely ordained means of conveying spiritual insight.
Audience members trust the speaker’s religious authority and sincerity.
Listening attentively with writing tools implies active engagement and reverence.

explicit_propositions.text: The church is not a physical building but a body of believers.
Paul referred to the church in someone's house, indicating the church is not defined by architecture.
The purpose of the church includes teaching biblical doctrine, fellowship, observance of the Lord's Supper, prayer, witnessing, and worship.
Acts 2:42 outlines the foundational purposes of the church: continuing steadfastly in apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.
Worship occurs when the church engages in doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer collectively.
The church is the spiritual body of Christ, with Jesus as its head.
Jesus Christ is the head of the church, not any human leader, organization, or political entity.
All believers in Jesus Christ from Pentecost to the rapture constitute the universal church.
Salvation involves the Holy Spirit’s work in regeneration, indwelling, sealing, and baptizing the believer into the body of Christ.
A person who does not have the Holy Spirit does not belong to Christ.

assumptions.text: True worship requires substance over spectacle and prioritizes spiritual engagement over entertainment.
Physical buildings are secondary to the spiritual reality of the church community.
The Holy Spirit is essential and non-negotiable in the process of salvation.
Human leaders and institutions should not be elevated above Christ in authority or significance.
Spiritual depth and doctrinal integrity outweigh emotional appeal and cultural trends in church practice.
The church’s primary mission is evangelism and discipleship, not social or recreational functions.
People can be spiritually deceived by superficial religious experiences lacking genuine transformation.
The universality of the church transcends race, class, gender, nationality, and socioeconomic status.
Divine revelation and scriptural authority supersede tradition, popularity, or institutional norms.
The current crisis context (e.g., pandemic) heightens urgency for authentic faith and proclamation of the Gospel.
